What if a lead comes in with no clear source?
Some leads arrive direct, with no trail, for example when they type your address in. We label those as direct or unknown rather than guessing, so the numbers stay honest.
Is source tracking allowed under privacy laws?
We use standard analytics and link tags that follow consent settings. Your site needs a cookie notice where your region requires one, and we check yours is working with the tags.
Which tools do you work with?
Google Analytics, Tag Manager, HubSpot, Zoho, Pipedrive, Google Sheets and common form tools. Tell us what you use, and we confirm before we begin.

desc:
Lead source tracking setup records where each enquiry came from, whether search, an ad, social media, a referral or an email link. Ecom Swift LLC sets up tagged links, hidden form fields and analytics goals, then tests every route with real clicks.

## What is lead source tracking?

Lead source tracking is the practice of attaching the origin of a visitor to the form they submit. When someone arrives through a link, the page remembers where they came from. When they send a form, that information travels with their name and message into your inbox, sheet or CRM.

With it, a lead is no longer just "John asked for a quote." It becomes "John, from the spring email, clicked the green button and asked for a quote."

## Why untracked leads hide your best channels

Without source data, every channel looks the same. You may be paying for ads that bring no one while a quiet referral link brings your best customers. You might also praise a source that delivers plenty of leads, none of whom buy.

Guessing leads to wasted budget and neglected channels. Tracking replaces that guesswork with a record. You can ask a simple question, such as "Which channel sent last month's leads?" and get an answer you can check.

## How tracking improves your decisions

Good tracking lets you move time and money toward what works. When you can compare channels, you can drop a source that only produces noise and put more effort into one that produces real conversations. It also helps when you test a new campaign, because you can tell whether its leads truly came from it.

Tracking does not create leads by itself. Its value is in the decisions it supports. The numbers are only as good as the setup behind them, which is why testing each route matters so much.

## What a great tracking setup includes

- Consistent tags on links, so campaigns are named the same way every time.
- Hidden fields on forms that capture source and campaign.
- Analytics goals for form submissions and bookings.
- A clean place to see leads and their source, such as a CRM field or sheet.
- Click tracking for phone numbers and email links.
- The source shown in the alert email you receive.
- A check that your consent banner behaves correctly.
- Connection of ad platform conversions where relevant.
- Guidance for call tracking numbers if calls matter to you.
- A simple dashboard that groups leads by source.

## What we do

We start by listing every way a lead can reach you: forms, bookings, phone numbers and email addresses. We agree on a naming system for sources and campaigns, then add link tags and hidden form fields so the details are captured. In your analytics tool we set up goals that count real enquiries.

We route the source into your CRM or a lead sheet and add it to your alert emails. Higher packages cover more forms, tagged links for several campaigns, phone click tracking, a consent banner check and ad platform connections. The largest package adds a live dashboard and guidance on call tracking. Finally we test each route with real clicks from different sources and confirm that the right label arrives each time.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Use the same naming pattern for every campaign.
- Tag every link you place in emails, ads and social profiles.
- Check the source on a few real leads each month.
- Record which leads became customers.
- Respect your visitors' privacy choices.

**Avoid:**
- Changing tag names halfway through a campaign.
- Trusting a number you have never tested.
- Tracking more details than you need.
- Treating "direct" as a real channel without investigating.
- Forgetting to track the forms on secondary pages.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a business that advertises in several places and cannot tell which one works. It also suits a company with a CRM that currently shows no source for most contacts. An owner planning a first paid campaign will gain a reliable record from the first day.

## What we need from you

Send the links to your forms and pages, a list of the channels you use, and the names of your analytics and CRM tools. We never need passwords. Access is given to us as a collaborator, staff or developer user in the tools involved, and everything we set up remains in your own accounts.
